generator.note: Every dimension below is a module constant in that script or a measurement of the shipped STEP. --check rebuilds from those constants and compares topology and volume-level facts; it never compares bytes, because the STEP header carries a write timestamp.

description: Suspension wishbone / A-arm. Two coaxial chassis-side bushing eyes on the y pivot axis fork through two swept arms with opposite out-of-plane profiles, tied by one swept cross-brace, into a single upright-side ball-joint boss. Frame: +x outboard toward the upright, +y the chassis pivot axis (fore-aft), +z up. SI metres.

dimensions_m.measurement: tight bounding box via BRepBndLib::AddOptimal and BRepGProp volume of tests/fixtures/parts/wishbone.step after reopening it; OpenCASCADE's default 1e-7 m box gap has been removed from each bound.

wall_thickness.method: inward ray cast along the area-weighted vertex normal against the full tessellation of the reopened STEP
wall_thickness.thinnest_location: the bushing annulus at both eyes: eye_outer 0.030 - bore 0.008 = 0.022 m
wall_thickness.why_it_is_a_first_class_dimension: the mesher snaps boundary nodes to the exact BRep inside a band of 1.5 * fill_h, so a wall thinner than that band lets both sides snap onto each other and the skin goes non-manifold. An earlier 24/9.5 mm eye and 28/12 mm boss left a 14.5 mm minimum wall and failed the product fill guard at h = 8 mm and h = 16 mm.

load.resultant_direction_note: 32.005 degrees from vertical, tilted inboard (-x). Vertical plus lateral, no invented fore-aft component.

derivation.case: linear-elastic proof load for a suspension control-arm showcase
derivation.basis: 10 × the rounded 4.717 kN combined bump/cornering design vector
derivation.purpose: Produces a visibly legible but still elastic distributed stress field on the two-sleeve/one-boss load path.
derivation.status: authored numerical proof load, explicitly not a measured vehicle event

hand_check.linearity: The solver is linear elastostatic: multiplying the conserved resultant by 10 multiplies stress and physical displacement by exactly 10 while leaving the ZZ relative indicator unchanged.
hand_check.solver_probe: The verified h=5.5 mm tet4 probe with these distributed interfaces produced 3.316 MPa at 4.717 kN, so the exact linear 10× proof-load expectation is 33.160 MPa before the final take is regenerated.
hand_check.status: probe-derived expectation, not substituted for the final manifest

load.description: Conserved resultant distributed over the complete outer boss sleeve. Two separated outer-sleeve supports plus one off-plane loaded boss produce a non-uniform bending-plus-torsion field while avoiding a point or edge singularity masquerading as material stress.

mesh.h_rationale: 0.0055 m keeps the 1.5 * fill_h snap band at 0.00825 m, 2.67x below the measured 0.02207 m minimum wall. Geometry and support/load grading are disabled for the verified uniform fill; exact support/load regions still drive boundary conditions. Element spans: bushing wall 4.01, boss wall 4.36, brace diameter 4.73, arm diameter 6.18. h_rel is 0.0114 of the 0.4829 m bbox diagonal. The full ZZ field is reported without implying a hidden remesh.

boundary_node_supply_at_h.support_outer_sleeve_each: order of 598 surface triangles and 299 nodes; 34.27 elements around by 8.73 along
boundary_node_supply_at_h.loaded_outer_boss: order of 847 surface triangles and 423 nodes; 38.84 elements around by 10.91 along
boundary_node_supply_at_h.purpose: shows neither support nor loaded regions resolve to a starved patch

mesh.status: High-resolution linear verification solve with distributed interfaces. Measured cells, DOF, quality and achieved error belong in manifest.json.

region_selection.method: The GUI grows region ids by flood-filling the display tessellation across shared edges while adjacent facet normals stay within 30 degrees (src/pipeline/src/scene.cpp Model::load), over the per-face triangle soup built in TopExp face order at deflection 5e-4 * bbox diagonal and angular deflection 0.2 rad (src/geom/src/cad_model.cpp). Replaying that exact algorithm on the shipped STEP gives 11 regions from 15 CAD faces: region 3 merges the two arms, the brace and the two inboard eye annuli, because the arms now blend into those annuli tangentially (junction interior angle 150 to 203 degrees, i.e. G1-smooth, so the 30-degree fill crosses it). Region id therefore no longer equals CAD face index, and the mapping above is explicit.

region_id_map.3: both arms + brace + both inboard eye annuli (merged, smooth blends)

region_selection.verification: GUI probes completed successfully with fix 5; fix 6; loadface 0. Regions are verified against the built product rather than left as predictions.
region_selection.area_keys: Boss outer sleeve analytic area 0.0128176980 m2; each eye outer sleeve 0.00904778684 m2. The two equal support regions are intentionally interchangeable because both are fixed.
region_selection.why_the_interfaces_survive: Each selected outer sleeve is one uninterrupted cylindrical region bounded by 90-degree annular edges. The 30-degree region flood therefore does not escape into a bore or neighboring arm.
region_selection.surface_quality: Worst convex edge 77.98 degrees, worst re-entrant crotch 290.44 degrees, measured over every tessellated edge. No knife edge, no tangential cusp, and no non-adjacent CAD face pair in contact, so there is no coincident-skin site anywhere on the part.

checks_enforced_by_generator: valid BRep, exactly one solid, positive volume, before and after the bores are cut
all three bore axes classify OUT along their whole sleeve length, and wall material classifies IN just outside each bore
exactly three cylindrical faces at the two bore radii, each at full sleeve area, so no bore was interrupted by a boolean
both arms exceed 0.012 m of out-of-plane excursion from the plane through the three eye centres, with opposite signs, so the fork is never coplanar
each arm spine travels at least 0.015 m in z

measured_out_of_plane_m.note: Signed peak distance from the plane through the two eye centres and the boss centre. Opposite signs are the numeric statement that this is a three-dimensional fork and not a perforated plate. The spines are unchanged from the first revision; only member and ring radii moved.
